title: Integrated Security & Compliance Playbook: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence Workflows, Risk Exceptions
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary:

This document consolidates Redwood Inference’s security and compliance controls across RBAC & authentication, audit logging, data residency & retention, secure SDLC practices, incident response for security events, compliance evidence collection workflows, and risk/exception handling. It is intended for security, SRE, infra, platform, and product engineering teams responsible for implementing and operating production services.

Goals:
- Define consistent RBAC and auth patterns across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Ensure tamper-evident audit trails with clear retention and access policies.
- Provide prescriptive data residency and retention settings aligned to customer contracts and regulations.
- Embed security controls into the SDLC with measurable gates.
- Standardize incident response procedures and evidence collection for compliance audits.
- Document risk exception process with approval and review cadence.

1) Ownership and Scope
- Document owner: Security Team (owner: Maya Chen).
- Operational owners: eng-sre (incident response & monitoring), eng-infra (log collection & storage), eng-platform (RBAC integration, console controls), product (compliance requirements for features).
- Scope: All Redwood-managed control plane services (api-gateway, redwood-auth, redwood-iam), production data paths, hosted API endpoints, Dedicated control plane components, and Private deployment support guidance.

2) RBAC & Authentication
- Principles:
  - Least privilege by default.
  - Role-based assignments, with attribute-based policy overrides where required (e.g., customer tenant isolation).
  - Centralized identity provider (IdP): Okta (SSO + SCIM) for corporate identity and service accounts federated via OIDC for machine identities.

- Roles & Typical Mappings (high level):
  - security-admin: security team, full access to audit/evidence portal, policy management.
  - infra-admin: eng-infra, ability to manage logging infra and cloud permissions.
  - platform-operator: eng-platform, can deploy control plane and update RBAC mappings.
  - service-owner: owning product/infra service owners with write access to their service config.
  - readonly-auditor: compliance/legal with read-only views into audit data and evidence.

- Implementation details:
  - Redwood-iam service: central RBAC engine that evaluates policies for API/console access. Service name: redwood-iam (kubernetes deployment: redwood-iam-prod).
  - Authentication: Okta SSO -> OIDC tokens exchanged for short-lived internal JWTs (TTL: 1h). Service accounts use OIDC with audience claim set to redwood-internal.
  - MFA: required for all interactive accounts with access to prod (Okta MFA enforced).
  - SCIM provisioning: automated group sync for role bindings; manual overrides require a security-admin approval ticket.
  - RBAC Change Controls: any role binding change in the prod-redwood namespace must go through the change-management workflow and be approved by an infra-admin + security-admin for >24h permissions grant.
  - Privileged Session Auditing: console sessions for elevated roles are recorded (session metadata + command logs) and stored in the audit log pipeline.

- Access Review Cadence:
  - Quarterly automated attestation for all privileged roles. Responsible: security + people-ops.

3) Audit Logging
- Goals: capture a tamper-evident, searchable trail for authentication, authorization decisions, configuration changes, data access, and administrative actions.

- Sources of logs:
  - redwood-auth: auth events (login, token issuance, revocation).
  - redwood-iam: policy evaluations, role changes, SCIM provisioning events.
  - api-gateway: request/response metadata (headers, latency, response codes) for control plane APIs.
  - service-admin consoles and CLI tooling: command execution logs and session metadata.
  - infra components: Kubernetes audit logs, cloud IAM changes, terraform runs from CICD.

- Collection & Pipeline:
  - Collector: audit-log-collector (daemonset) forwards normalized logs to Kafka topic audits-prod.
  - Processing: log-transformer jobs (k8s) add canonical fields and compute integrity hashes.
  - Storage: immutable log archives in s3://redwood-audit-archive/{region}/{year}/ and hot indices in Elasticsearch: audits-prod-YYYY.MM.
  - Integrity: each daily archive is hashed and a manifest is written to the integrity service (integrity-store), which writes a signed manifest to AWS KMS-protected bucket.

- Retention SLOs & Policies:
  - Hot index retention (Elasticsearch): 90 days.
  - Nearline archive (S3, searchable via Athena): 2 years for standard customers.
  - Long-term retention (compliance/enterprise customers): up to 7 years per contract; configuration is per-customer and implemented via lifecycle rules and encrypted vaulted buckets.
  - Tamper-detection: manifests retained for 10 years.

- Access controls & Monitoring:
  - Only readonly-auditor and security-admin roles may query raw audit archives. Ad-hoc access requires approval ticket and is logged.
  - SLO: audit log ingestion latency < 30s 99th percentile for control plane events. Responsible: eng-sre.
  - Alerts: gaps in ingestion, integrity verification failures, or unexpected deletions trigger P1 to incident-response-security channel.

4) Data Residency & Retention
- Principles:
  - Customer data must remain within the customer-selected region(s) for hosted deployments unless explicit cross-region replication is requested in contract.
  - Control-plane logs and metadata are separated from customer content traces where feasible; customer content retention follows contract/tenant policy.

- Region mapping & defaults:
  - EU customers default to eu-west-1 region clusters; NA customers default to us-east-1. APAC options provided on request.
  - Storage endpoints: s3://redwood-eu-logs, s3://redwood-us-logs, and dedicated enterprise buckets per contract.

- Retention policy (default):
  - Control plane logs/metadata: 2 years (nearline) with 90-day hot window.
  - Customer content (generated text, embeddings): default 30 days; enterprise customers may opt into 0 retention or configurable retention up to 7 years.
  - Backup snapshots: encrypted, cross-region replication disabled by default for EU-resident buckets.

- Implementation checklist for new customer onboarding (minimum):
  1. Confirm residency requirement in contract and record in onboarding playbook.
  2. Provision region-specific buckets and IAM roles.
  3. Configure logging pipeline to route tenant events to the tenant’s region.
  4. Validate via end-to-end test (sample payload, verify location + KMS encryption).

5) Secure SDLC (Software Development Life Cycle)
- Objective: ensure security gates are enforced across code, infra-as-code, and deployment pipelines.

- Required controls in CI/CD (applies to all repos in github.com/redwood):
  - Mandatory code review: PRs require 2 approvers for security-sensitive repos; 1 approver for low-risk repos.
  - Automated scans: SAST (semgrep), SCA (Dependabot + Snyk), container image scanning (Trivy), and licensed vulnerability scanners for binary dependencies.
  - Secrets scanning: pre-commit and CI checks (git-secrets + checkov) and periodic repo-wide secret sweeps.
  - IaC checks: terraform fmt/checkov/lint, policy-as-code with OPA checks in pipeline (rego policies).
  - Deployment gating: canary deploy + automated integration tests in staging; security smoke tests must pass before production rollout.

- Branch protection & signing:
  - Enforce branch protection rules on main and release branches; require signed commits for infra repos.

- Security release checklist (pre-production):
  1. SAST and SCA scans completed, no critical findings.
  2. Dependency upgrade/justification for medium findings logged in PR.
  3. Secrets check clear.
  4. Rollback plan & runbook attached to release.
  5. Post-deploy monitoring dashboards and SLO checks in place.

- Training & Developer Support:
  - Annual secure-coding training required for engineers.
  - Security champions program: one champion per engineering team.

6) Incident Response — Security Procedures
- Goals: detect, contain, eradicate, recover, and preserve evidence with clear internal and external communication paths.

- Detection & Triage:
  - Sources: IDS/IPS alerts, SIEM detections (Splunk), anomaly detection from runtime telemetry (latency, error spikes), customer reports.
  - Triage owners: on-call eng-sre + security on-call. Use incident triage template in PagerDuty.

- Response phases (high level):
  1. Identification: assign incident ID (IR-YYYYMMDD-####).
  2. Containment: isolate affected services (eg: remove route from load balancer, revoke service tokens), preserve snapshots.
  3. Forensics & Evidence Preservation: create immutable snapshots of relevant systems, export audit logs slice, record hashes in integrity-store.
  4. Eradication: apply patches, rotate keys and secrets, revoke compromised credentials.
  5. Recovery: restore services from clean images and verify with smoke tests.
  6. Post-Incident Review: publish an internal postmortem within 7 business days.

- Evidence preservation checklist (security incidents):
  - Snapshot VM/Pod state and persist to s3://redwood-forensics/{incident-id}/snapshots/ (encrypt with KMS key: arn:aws:kms:...:redwood-forensics).
  - Export relevant audit log ranges to s3://redwood-forensics/{incident-id}/logs/ and compute sha256 manifests.
  - Preserve network captures (pcap) if applicable in s3://redwood-forensics/{incident-id}/pcaps/ with access restricted to security and forensics engineers.
  - Document chain of custody in the incident ticket (Jira) and sign-off by security lead.

- Communication:
  - Internal: Incident channel (Slack): #incident-<id>-security, mandatory initial incident brief within 30 minutes.
  - External: Customer-facing incident notes via status.redwood.com and direct email for impacted customers. Legal and PR involved for incidents meeting breach criteria.

- SLAs for response:
  - Acknowledge P1 security incidents within 15 minutes.
  - Initial containment actions completed within 2 hours for production-impacting incidents.

7) Compliance Evidence Workflows
- Purpose: provide repeatable, auditable workflows for collecting artifacts required by external audits (SOC2, ISO27001, customer audits).

- Evidence types & storage locations:
  - Policy documents and attestations: Confluence export snapshots stored in s3://redwood-compliance-evidence/policies/{date}/.
  - Configuration snapshots (RBAC snapshots, IAM policies): s3://redwood-compliance-evidence/config/{service}/{date}/.
  - Audit log extracts: s3://redwood-compliance-evidence/audit/{tenant}/{date}/ (encrypted).
  - Incident evidence packages: s3://redwood-compliance-evidence/incidents/{incident-id}/.
  - Access proofs (attestation logs): s3://redwood-compliance-evidence/attestations/{quarter}/.

- Evidence collection process (numbered):
  1. Auditor request received: create compliance-audit-{REQUEST-ID} ticket and assign a compliance engineer.
  2. Scope scoping call: determine scope, retention window, tenant IDs.
  3. Evidence pull: compliance engineer runs the evidence-extractor tool (internal CLI) to generate a signed evidence bundle.
  4. Bundle upload: signed bundle uploaded to s3://redwood-compliance-evidence/{request-id}/ and a link posted to the auditor portal (internal).
  5. Audit trail: record hash of the bundle in integrity-store and update the ticket with chain-of-custody.
  6. Access: auditor access is time-limited (default 14 days) and logged via presigned URLs.

- Evidence retention and disposition:
  - Audit evidence for SOC2 assessments: retain 3 years.
  - Customer-specific audit artifacts: per contract (document in onboarding checklist).
  - Disposal: automated lifecycle transitions to Glacier and deletion per retention schedule; deletion must be approved by security and legal for artifacts older than 7 years.

8) Risk & Exceptions
- When teams cannot meet a security control (technical constraint, customer requirement), the risk exception process must be used.

- Exception request form (minimum fields):
  - service_name, owner, control_id, requested_deviation, business_justification, compensating_controls, duration, mitigations, risk_owner, approvers.

- Approval workflow:
  1. Submit form in the risk-exception Jira project.
  2. Security reviews and proposes compensating controls.
  3. Legal reviews (if customer data affected).
  4. Exec sign-off required for exceptions > 90 days or where residual risk is high.
  5. Approved exceptions are added to the risk register and reviewed monthly until closed.

- Monitoring & Renewal:
  - All exceptions auto-expire at the requested duration; renewal requires explicit re-approval.
  - Quarterly exception inventory report published to execs.

9) Appendix
- Contact list:
  - Security on-call: security-oncall@redwood.example (PagerDuty)
  - eng-sre on-call: sre-oncall@redwood.example (PagerDuty)
  - Compliance engineering: compliance@redwood.example
  - Evidence portal owner: infra-compliance@redwood.example

- Key service names and resources:
  - redwood-iam (RBAC engine), redwood-auth, audit-log-collector, integrity-store, evidence-extractor, s3://redwood-compliance-evidence, s3://redwood-audit-archive, s3://redwood-forensics.

- Change history:
  - 2025-11-12: Created by Maya Chen.
  - 2026-01-20: Updated audit retention SLOs (eng-sre).
  - 2026-03-04: Published with updated incident response SLAs and evidence workflow improvements (reviewed by Jordan Lee, Priya Nair, Luca Romano).

Definitions:
- Customer content: any text or embeddings provided by or generated for a customer.
- Control plane: Redwood-managed services that implement API, orchestration, and RBAC functionality.

End of document.
